question: Who will win the 2026 Brazilian Presidential election?

calls.reasoning: Flávio led round one 47.03-45.16; ~7.8% leftover vote is mostly centre-right (Caiado endorsed Flávio Oct 6; Cury neutral; Renan Santos neutral). Since 1989 the first-round runner-up has never won a Brazilian runoff. Pre-election polls overstated Lula by ~5 pts on margin, yet the Quaest runoff poll (Oct 2-3) is only Flávio 44-42, inside the margin, so Lula retains a real path via mobilising record abstention (21%). Polymarket prices Flávio at 84% on a matching winner contract (~$174M volume); I shade slightly toward the tied-poll uncertainty.
calls.dossier:
- First round Oct 4 2026: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) 47.03%, Lula (PT) 45.16% of valid votes; ~7.8% to ~10 other candidates described as largely centre-right (Al Jazeera, NBC, Oct 5 2026).
- Abstention 21.08%, highest since 1998 (NBC, Oct 2026).
- Pre-election private surveys had Lula leading round one by ~3 pts; result was Flávio +1.9, i.e. polls overstated Lula's margin by ~5 pts (NBC).
- Quaest/Globo runoff poll Oct 2-3 (n=3,702, ±2pp): Flávio 44%, Lula 42% total votes, a technical tie (CNN Brasil, Oct 3 2026). Datafolha runoff poll due Oct 8 and AtlasIntel Oct 9 (Brasil de Fato, Oct 6).
- 3rd place Augusto Cury (Avante) 2.89%: says he will stay silent and leave politics (Agência Brasil, Oct 2026). 4th Renan Santos 2.24%: backs neither but projects a Flávio win. Ronaldo Caiado formally endorsed Flávio on Oct 6; Zema declared explicit support (Gazeta do Povo / search summary).
- Historical: in Brazilian runoffs since 1989 the first-round runner-up has never won (Al Jazeera, citing analysts). 2022: Lula led R1 48.4-43.2 and won the runoff 50.9-49.1, with Bolsonaro gaining more from leftover votes but not enough to overturn the lead.
- For Lula: incumbency, the runoff poll is within the margin of error, room to mobilise high-abstention Northeast voters, and the campaign is retooling its social media.
- For Flávio: the leftover vote leans right, endorsements so far favour him, he beat the polls in round one, and observers cite evangelical support and security/inflation concerns.
- Status quo: the first-round leader goes on to win.
- Resolves off the official winner of the Oct 25 2026 runoff (TSE), per linked Metaculus Q45996.
- Event window: runoff Oct 25 2026; as of Oct 6, ~19 days remain before the vote.
- Searched but not found: Datafolha/AtlasIntel runoff numbers (not yet published), Ciro Gomes' runoff stance.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Brazilian presidential runoffs 1989-2022 — first-round leader won all 7; broader Latin American runoffs ~70-80% leader wins. Flávio led 47.03-45.16 with only ~7.8% to other candidates, mostly right-leaning; Caiado and Zema endorsed Flávio, Cury and Renan neutral. Lula needs ~62% of residual votes or a turnout shift. Counter: runoff polls were near ties (Quaest Oct 3 had Flávio 44-42 total), Lula is the incumbent, and abstention (21%) was high, so mobilization could matter. Polymarket (same contract, ~$174M volume) has Flávio at 84%; Manifold has Lula at 16%. I land near the market.
calls.dossier:
- First round Oct 4 2026 (Wikipedia/TSE): Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) 47.03% (56.1M votes), Lula (PT) 45.16% (53.9M); others combined ~7.8% of valid votes. Turnout 78.92%; abstention 21.08%, the highest since 1998 (Americas Quarterly, Oct 5).
- Congress: PL won ~121 Chamber seats (+22) and large Senate gains; analysts (Traumann) called it an 'anti-PT tsunami'; Brian Winter (AQ) compared it to the 2024 US election (AQ, Oct 5).
- Endorsements (InfoMoney/Ric, Oct 5-6): Caiado and Zema back Flávio; Augusto Cury (3rd place) neutral; Renan Santos neutral but said Flávio has 'already won'.
- Pre-first-round runoff polls: Datafolha Oct 1 had Lula 45-40 (valid votes per NBC); Quaest Oct 2-3 (n=3,702, ±2) had Flávio 44, Lula 42 in total votes, 13% blank/null. Flávio's first-round share was above what pre-election polls showed.
- Upcoming polls: Datafolha releases Oct 8 (n=2,520); AtlasIntel first runoff poll Oct 9 (Brasil de Fato, Oct 6).
- Lula is the 80-year-old incumbent with a strong Northeast base; possible upside from mobilizing abstainers.
- Base rate: Brazilian runoffs 1989, 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022 — first-round leader won all 7. In Latin American runoffs generally, comeback wins by the runner-up happen in a minority of cases (for example Peru 2021 and 2016, Argentina 2015 and 2023, Colombia 2022 runner-ups who were close).
- Arithmetic: Lula needs ~4.85 of the ~7.8 residual points (~62%) if turnout is unchanged; the residual is mostly center-right/right.
- Resolution: resolves on the official TSE runoff winner, per the linked Metaculus question 45996.
- Event window: runoff Oct 25 2026, resolution ~Oct 26; as of Oct 6 the 3-week runoff campaign has barely started (~10% elapsed).
- Searched but not found: runoff polls fielded after Oct 4; any Lula-side endorsements from eliminated candidates.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Brazilian presidential runoffs 1989-2022, where the first-round leader won 7 of 7; Latin American runner-up comebacks happen in a minority of cases. Flávio led 47.03-45.16, and the ~7.8% residual is mostly centre-right (Caiado and Zema endorse him; Cury and Renan Santos neutral), so Lula needs ~62% of it or a turnout shift. Round-one polls understated Flávio by ~5pts on margin. Lula's path is incumbency, a tied Quaest poll (44-42 Flávio) and mobilising record 21% abstention. Polymarket's matching winner contract has Flávio at 0.84 (Manifold has Lula at 0.16); I land at 0.83.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: the R1 result, endorsements, the 7/7 historical record and the tied Quaest poll. The only factual discrepancy is the size of Polymarket's volume: runs cited ~$174M, but the harness listing shows ~$17.55M and a close date of 2026-10-05, so the 0.84 price may be stale but is still a deep, matching winner contract. No post-R1 runoff polls exist yet (Datafolha Oct 8, AtlasIntel Oct 9), so that question cannot be settled. The remaining dispute (0.16-0.20 for Lula) is judgment about how much weight the tied poll and abstention mobilisation deserve against history and a right-leaning residual. Given the R1 polling error in Flávio's favour, I take 0.17 for Lula.
